author: DPA
title: Georgia summons German envoy over alleged 'interference' - NewsBreak
text:
By DPA ,
3 hours ago
The Georgian Foreign Ministry on Wednesday summoned German Ambassador Peter Fischer over his repeated criticism of the government's increasingly authoritarian trajectory.
"During the meeting, the Ambassador was reminded that, pursuant to Article 41(1) of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, members of a diplomatic mission are obliged to respect the laws and regulations of the receiving state and are likewise required not to interfere in the internal affairs of the host country," the ministry said in a statement.
"The Georgian side expressed concern regarding attempts to encourage a radical agenda within the country, which are inconsistent with the principles of democracy and contribute to the aggravation of societal polarization," it added.
The German Foreign Office rejected the accusations, describing the summons as "baseless."
"We firmly reject the continuing aggressive rhetoric by representatives of [ruling party] Georgian Dream towards the German Ambassador in Tblisi," it said in a post on Bluesky.
According to the Foreign Office, Fischer "represents the position of the Federal Government & acts in full compliance with the Vienna Convention."
It comes after Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze accused Fischer of interfering in the country's internal affairs two weeks ago.
"Fischer is such a tragic figure that it would be a gift for him to be expelled," Kobakhidze told the Interpressnews news agency.
The German diplomat has attracted criticism for attending court hearings against members of the opposition.
Fischer also faced censure from the Georgian government for months after he rented the house of an opposition politician.
Georgian Dream declared itself the winner of the country's controversial parliamentary election late last year, sparking weeks of mass protests in Tbilisi.
The election further strained relations between Tbilisi and Brussels, with the Georgian government subsequently suspending accession negotiations to join the EU.
The EU delegation in Tbilisi has expressed solidarity with Fischer in the latest dispute.
